fact: The same study reports, from officials interviewed November 2024 to January 2025, that headquarters had a Police Information Management System, described as a digital database for storing and managing police records including crime reports, case files and investigations; it says nothing of stations entering records in it, and elsewhere says the occurrence book and dockets are paper.

The study says the Zambia Police Strategic Plan 2023-2026 and the service's training policy give guidelines for developing an e-record management system for all the service's electronic records and call for rolling out ICT infrastructure; an official said in December 2024 that most of the plan's targets had not been met for lack of funds.

The study names the Zambia Police Service's Technical Services Directorate, the Ministry of Home Affairs and Internal Security and the SMART Zambia Institute as those building and running the police's electronic systems, with the police as end user and adviser on design.

Citing the Yellow Books, the study gives budget allocations for e-Government at police headquarters of US$56,896,732 in 2021, US$57,136,364 in 2022, US$77,072,374 in 2023 and US$94,708,524 in 2024, which it says was under 35% of what was needed, with no line for ICT equipment or ICT training; the figures are for e-Government at headquarters as a whole, not for a records system.
